title: Drummer Wilbur Kirk leaves for Noble Sissle
summary: The first drummer, Wilbur Kirk, and the guitarist leave to join Noble Sissle, who came to St. Louis in 1935.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And, we thought of it as being a nice public relations sort of thing, to please the patrons and keep them coming to the nightclub. So the band opened and the band was a riot. Saturday nights you couldn't get them in there. They were always having to turn away 50 or 100 people. The floor shows were a hit, out of this world. Now the first drummer when we came back, we hired a boy named Wilbur Kirk. Wilbur Kirk was a very fine drummer, he knew the fundamentals of the drums.
He played with us that whole season. Noble Sissle came through town and Wilbur Kirk joined Noble Sissle and so did our guitarist.
And We wished them well and there was no hard feelings or anything like that. They went their way and we stayed here, and -- and kept our way.
Kirk got his break with Billy Rose, didn't he?

That's right. The -- the band that Kirk joined the Noble Sissle band, opened at Billy Rose's Diamond Horseshoe in New York and they played there several years, didn't they? They played there four or five years.
Then they kept him as the house drummer.
That's right, he played the shows so well they kept him as a house drummer. They sure did.
That's when he first brought Lena Horne there too, isn't it?
Noble Sissle. And a boy named Banks, singer. And they played -- they played here and they played out in a -- in a park, Satter's Park.
Sarter's Park, that's right. That was in 1935, when they came, you see. When they came -- Noble Sissle came here in 1935, so we -- we opened the Club in 1934, and went through the holidays into 1935.
We would open in September and close in April.
Close April, sometime in May. Sometimes in May, most the times in April.
